challenge.name: The Heatwave Blind Spot
challenge.description: A sudden heatwave has shifted demand for seasonal articles, and the current forecast is missing the mark. #model_monica# wants to automate the evaluation harness to test new weather features rapidly, while #requirements_reuben# wants to keep it manual to ensure every test case is rigorously documented before any model change is considered.

output.content: The manual drift check hand over is a bottleneck for the seasonal articles right now. Every time a heatwave shifts the demand for garden furniture or ice cream, we are waiting on a human to verify the data quality before the model can even see the new weather signals. Automating that hand over would let us catch those shifts in real time. The more automated that verification step becomes, the faster we can feed clean, reliable data into the evaluation harness. This directly supports the goal of testing new weather features without the current delay. I am pushing for this because a faster, automated check means we can respond to market changes immediately, and more of that speed is always better for the team.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states that 'more of that speed is always better,' indicating that exceeding the minimum requirement for automation would increase satisfaction.
